metadata.summary: Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday.
metadata.content: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around Man Utd's under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick being given the opportunity to turn current situation around with the 13-time Premier League winners currently on an eight-game winless run in all competitions and one point above the relegation zone Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Tuesday 27 October 2026 14:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan is at Manchester United's Carrington training ground with the significant news that Michael Carrick will remain in charge heading into the weekend Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday. The under-pressure United head coach was thought to be on the brink after Sunday's crushing 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, but he and the players are being given the chance to turn the current situation around. United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, were at Carrington discussing Carrick's future on Monday. It is understood they had already been considering alternatives for the head coach role. However, Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision has been taken to give him at least one more match. messages.text: Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test late due to neck injury

metadata.summary: Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test decider against South Africa in Cape Town after it was confirmed late on Tuesday morning that the batter had not fully recovered from a neck injury.
metadata.content: Australia vs South Africa: Steve Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test due to neck injury | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Australia vs South Africa: Steve Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test due to neck injury Steve Smith was a late injury omission for Australia ahead of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa on Tuesday; the 37-year-old had been set to play at Cape Town for the first time since the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal; watch the third Test live on Sky Sports Tuesday 27 October 2026 09:20, UK Image: Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test against South Africa Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test decider against South Africa in Cape Town after it was confirmed late on Tuesday morning that the batter had not fully recovered from a neck injury. Australia gave the 37-year-old a chance to prove his fitness ahead of the Test match, which would have seen Smith return to Cape Town for the first time since the infamous 'Sandpapergate' scandal at Newlands in 2018. Smith appeared to injure himself during his first spell at the crease during Australia's second Test defeat to South Africa in Gqeberha, in which the hosts levelled the series 1-1. metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton reveals he's 'lost out' in recent F1 races with set-up of his Ferrari car compared to Charles Leclerc | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton reveals he's 'lost out' in recent F1 races with set-up of his Ferrari car compared to Charles Leclerc Lewis Hamilton feels he's not optimised set-up of his Ferrari car recently which has cost him performance; Hamilton finished fourth in Sunday's US Grand Prix while Charles Leclerc was second; watch every session of the Mexico City GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports Tuesday 27 October 2026 07:48, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict on the on United States GP, as a dominant win for Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli leaves the Italian needing just two points from the Mexico GP to claim an historic first world title Lewis Hamilton has revealed he's "lost out" to Charles Leclerc through the set-up of his Ferrari car in recent races. Hamilton was outqualified by Leclerc at the United States Grand Prix and was unable to match his team-mate's impressive pace in the race on his way to fourth, while Leclerc finished second behind race-winner Kimi Antonelli. At the previous race in Singapore, Hamilton looked strong in qualifying until Q3 when he was beaten by Leclerc, and a similar pattern occurred in Austin where the seven-time world champion topped final practice, only to qualify fifth.
